structured_output.hypothesis: In measured cross-sectional stature-by-age data, the annualized height increment is highest in infancy, falls to a long, nearly steady, lower plateau in mid-childhood, rises to a clear second maximum in the early teens, and falls to near zero by the late teens.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using survey-weighted mean stature (NHANES, sexes separately) by age, compute annual increments in cm/yr. ALL of the following must hold in both sexes. (1) Infancy: the annualized increment from about 3 to 24 months of age is at least 1.5 times the mean increment over ages 6-9 years. (2) Steady childhood: increments for ages 5-10 years each lie within ±25% of their mean, and are all below the infancy increment. (3) Teen quickening: the maximum increment at ages 10-15 years exceeds the mean 6-9 year increment by at least 20%, and the age of that peak lies within 10-15 years. (4) Arrest: the mean increment over ages 18-20 years is below 1.0 cm/yr, and below 20% of the teen peak increment.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted in a sex if ANY of the following holds. The 3-24 month annualized increment is less than 1.5 times the mean 6-9 year increment. Any 5-10 year increment falls outside ±25% of the 5-10 year mean. The maximum 10-15 year increment is less than 1.2 times the mean 6-9 year increment, or the peak falls outside 10-15 years. The mean 18-20 year increment is 1.0 cm/yr or more.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'stature' and 'length' are mapped to measured recumbent length (under 2 years) and standing height (2 years and older). His 'babyhood' is about 0-2 years, 'early boyhood' is about 5-10 years, 'the growing age' (the early teens) is 10-15 years, and 'arrest' is 18-20 years. The 'curve of growth' is rendered as the annual increment (velocity) of sex-specific mean stature by age. Modern reinterpretation: NHANES is cross-sectional, so increments are differences between successive age-group means, not individual longitudinal velocities. Because individual timing of puberty varies, this can blur and lower the apparent peak. Thompson's 'almost steady' is operationalized as a ±25% band. NHANES does not measure birth length, so the infancy window starts at about 3 months. Sexes are analysed separately, with the quoted passage speaking of boys. NHANES pooled cycles (for example 1999-2018, using the examination weights WTMEC2YR) are used for sample size.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) – Body Measures (Examination data)
dataset.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES records measured stature, not self-reported. Its body measures files (BMX) give recumbent length (BMXRECUM) for infants and standing height (BMXHT) for older participants. Demographics files (DEMO) give age in years (RIDAGEYR), age in months (RIDAGEEX) and sex (RIAGENDR), and exam weights (WTMEC2YR) are provided. It spans infancy to adulthood in one survey, so it can test all four phases of the claim. Files are free downloads in SAS XPT format.
